records.region: Chihuahua, Mexico: western El Álamo valley and eastern interior plain through the Laguna El Diablo–El Sauz corridor to Encinillas.
records.geographic_disambiguation: El Sauz is directly printed on the selected lower receiving watercourse and listed among intermittent watercourses in the original municipal hydrography table. Full ordinary correspondence connects the selected El Álamo upper valley and intervening lake/playa floor to this receiving corridor and Encinillas. The candidate is a representative system identity, not a uniform name for every upper reach or lake component. No extra alias is established.
records.completion_scope: All 26 stored mainstem parts and both coincident endings have ordinary geographic correspondence. The original municipal map supplies distinct hydronyms and connected receiving geography, while independently acquired imagery covers the clipped western opening and complete fan/playa passages through the actual lake ending. No separate-basin gap or missing lake-to-feeder transfer remains at the required ordinary corridor scale.
records.supported_name_scope: El Sauz is directly printed on the selected lower receiving watercourse and listed among intermittent watercourses in the original municipal hydrography table. Full ordinary correspondence connects the selected El Álamo upper valley and intervening lake/playa floor to this receiving corridor and Encinillas. The candidate is a representative system identity, not a uniform name for every upper reach or lake component. No extra alias is established.

scope_limits: El Sauz is the representative receiving-system identity; El Álamo is a separate upper-reach name and the lakes are separate components.
The exact chosen opening name and precise El Álamo/El Sauz naming boundary are unestablished.
Municipal map generalization and the photographic floor do not certify individual banks, engineered channels, every field crossing or current hydraulic continuity.
Laguna El Diablo, Laguna Palomas and Encinillas are separate labels; no alias relationship is inferred.
Historical source classifications and imagery do not establish present lake extent, water level, flow permanence, salinity or water-management operations.
No official river length, naming registry status or Korean name has been verified.

terminal_review.source_terminal: The stored source ending is in the mapped Encinillas lake-interior setting after the final northwestward lake approach.
terminal_review.render_terminal: The rendered ending coincides with the same stored source endpoint and lake setting. No extension is added.
terminal_review.terminal_class_limit: Endorheic is retained as stored model metadata. The mapped lake and broad receiving floor establish ordinary terminal geography, without independently certifying a surveyed closure boundary or modern hydraulic operation.

records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative of the researched connected river and receiving floodplain/coastal corridor. Does not rename the bounded Villarteaga upper association or every tiny feeder.
records.completion_scope: Complete practical name/corridor correspondence at ordinary valley, floodplain, wetland and coastal scale. Exact banks, current wet threads, and every local hydronym boundary are outside this completion claim.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative of the researched connected river and receiving floodplain/coastal corridor. Does not rename the bounded Villarteaga upper association or every tiny feeder.

scope_limits: The forested opening is a terrain/valley correspondence; dense canopy and localized clouds prevent an exact small-channel trace or a separately named source.

The coarse selection locally cuts across bends and cultivated/wetland floodplain rather than reproducing every photographed meander. Ordinary receiving-corridor continuity is sufficient and is supported.
The Villarteaga usage is a bounded upper association. No claim of uniform scalar naming or formal alias over all selected parts is made.
Photographic mosaic dates and present river or drainage-management operations are not established.
The POMCA authorial prose is usable, but its borrowed IGAC map network is not used as substitute evidence for held hydrography.

bounded_name_observations.name: Río Villarteaga
bounded_name_observations.scope: The basin study associates the upper León with Villarteaga and its highway-bridge setting; no exact naming boundary, tiny opening name or whole-system alias is asserted.

bounded_name_observations.name: Golfo de Urabá
bounded_name_observations.scope: Named coastal destination of the León in authorial basin prose; not a river alias.

terminal_review.observation: The stored source endpoint lies in the lower river-mouth approach. The separately stored render endpoint extends northwest toward the inner-gulf coastal opening. Both belong to the visible connected mouth and coastal receiving setting, consistent with the study’s Golfo de Urabá destination. They are preserved separately; neither is promoted to an exact surveyed shoreline intersection or a present-flow measurement.

records.region: Chubut, Argentina: a north–south interior alluvial collector ending in a closed lake/playa floor; Laguna de Agnia is a bounded regional bibliographic lead.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: No permitted actually read source establishes a representative natural-river name for the full selected collector. A regional lake-study name is not promoted to a river identity.
records.geographic_disambiguation: North–south Chubut alluvial collector, through visible connected valleys and receiving floors to the actual interior lake/playa ending. Laguna de Agnia is bounded prior-catalogue regional context, not a selected river or exact lake-name assignment.
records.completion_scope: All29 selected mainstem parts have complete ordinary terrain/receiving-floor correspondence into an interior lake/playa. No representative natural-river name is supported by the permitted read sources; completed null name-scope hold. The optional Reato2020 original remained unread after an incomplete transfer, with its exact source stop preserved.
records.supported_name_scope: No permitted actually read source establishes a representative natural-river name for the full selected collector. A regional lake-study name is not promoted to a river identity.

scope_limits: No representative natural-river identity or true alias is supported by the permitted actually read material; candidate and all application names remain null.
The regional Laguna de Agnia catalogue context is not independently georeferenced to this precise photographed endpoint; it is preserved only as bounded lake-study context.

Fine channels can be faint or diffuse across dry alluvial and playa floors. Ordinary connected receiving-floor geography is supported without asserting a continuously wet thread or present hydraulic operation.
Individual imagery dates, exact current water extent, banks, channel positions and engineered drainage operation remain unverified.

Discovery-only mentions of Lonco Trapial, Mallín Blanco, Epul and other regional names were not promoted to selected reaches or aliases; unavailable or unresolved publications and unseen maps are excluded.

bounded_name_observations.name: Laguna de Agnia
bounded_name_observations.scope: The successfully read Reato2020 institutional catalogue identifies this named shallow-lake study in extra-Andean Chubut. The catalogue has no detailed selected-area cartography or coordinates, so it does not by itself georeference the name to the photographed endpoint and supplies no river alias. Exact lake-label correspondence remains a naming limitation, not a missing physical connection.

source_ending.ordinary_setting: Interior pale lake/playa receiving floor beside a darker western marginal drainage strip.

render_ending.ordinary_setting: The same interior receiving-floor position, separately retained from the source-ending description.

terminal_review.source_and_render_ending_relation: Coincident in the supplied selected metadata; no extension or repair.

records.region: Dominican Republic: Ozama upland and floodplain corridor to the Santo Domingo port/coastal mouth.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Supported representative receiving-system identity for the researched upland-to-coastal selection. This does not assert a uniform hydronym over the chosen small opening, every tributary, wetland channel or individual reach, and does not extend the selected beginning to the river’s natural source.
records.completion_scope: All25 stored parts of the single stage3 mainstem fragment were reviewed from the chosen upland opening through its ordinary receiving corridors, joins, floodplain and urban port/coastal ending. Independent municipal prose supports Río Ozama as the representative system. No material geographic transfer is left pending; local image visibility and exact-name-scope limits are preserved.
records.supported_name_scope: Supported representative receiving-system identity for the researched upland-to-coastal selection. This does not assert a uniform hydronym over the chosen small opening, every tributary, wetland channel or individual reach, and does not extend the selected beginning to the river’s natural source.

scope_limits: No exact natural-source or spring assignment for the selected first vertex; a representative system identity is not a reach-by-reach name assertion.

A few cloud, shadow and canopy patches obscure individual channel threads. The completed finding rests on ordinary visible valley/floodplain continuity with independent regional hydrologic prose, not continuous exact-bank tracing.
The municipal plan distinguishes Verde from Ozama and describes different headwater hills; no ambiguous headwater wording is promoted into a true alias.
Tributary relationships are supported in prose, but most individual photographed junctions are left unnamed rather than over-assigned.

Source and rendered endings differ and remain separately described at the harbor/coastal receiving setting. No exact bank, tidal limit, present water level, discharge, port operation or navigational condition is verified.
The optional history publication remains unavailable after its direct404; its search extracts and unread response body are excluded.
Formal registry and Korean naming remain unverified; no application or geometry change is authorized by this finding.

terminal_review.observation: The urban river continues southwest, meets a broad western tributary approach, then turns south through the port channel to the coastal opening. The rendered ending is at the inner harbor-mouth setting; the separate source ending lies slightly farther seaward at the coastal receiving opening. Both are preserved as distinct endpoint descriptions. The municipal plan independently names the Ozama receiving system and its Caribbean outlet, with San Soucí at the mouth. No exact shoreline, tidal boundary, present navigational depth or active-flow assertion is made.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
